maria: quick async — hitting a weird dim mismatch when we merge embeddings from two flows. Some results are 1536 dims, others 1024, and our downstream rerank crashes. Also seeing paginator cursor decode errors after an auth retry (cursor->decode error). anyone seen both together?

 sachin: model mismatch sounds likely. which model names are you calling? double-check the client `model=` param and any legacy aliases in config. 1536 = text-embedding-3-large, 1024 = older small variants. Also show the auth header you’re using (no creds in thread, just format).

 maria: minimal repro: calling our batch helper which wraps the SDK. header is `Authorization: Bearer ${REDWOOD_KEY}`. snippet:```# pseudo
client = RedwoodClient(model=cfg.model)
batcher.add(batch)
```
getting: `ValueError: embedding length mismatch (expected 1536, got 1024)` and occasionally `CursorDecodeError: invalid padding` after a 401 -> retry flow.

 olivia: two quick checks: 1) confirm `cfg.model` isn't being overridden by an env var or old alias; 2) our paginate cursor is urlsafe-base64 encoded JSON — if the retry path re-encodes an already-encoded cursor you get padding issues.

 julia: also verify dtype/shape in the batcher before send. we had a bug where lists of lists produced ragged numpy arrays which ended up being cast/trimmed. tiny check:```expected = 1536
for v in batch:
  if len(v) != expected:
    raise RuntimeError(f"dim mismatch {len(v)} != {expected}")
```
and ensure you `np.array(..., dtype=np.float32)` before sending.

 maria: thanks — found the config alias in our service config referencing `emb-small` (legacy). swapped to `emb-large` and dims align now. opened a PR to add the shape guard + fix cursor encode path: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/512

 ci-bot: CI checks queued for #512 — running unit tests

 devex-bot: quick note: embedding endpoints are non-streaming; rerank supports streamed scoring updates in the newer API but it doesn't affect embedding pagination.

 sachin: for the cursor bug, use urlsafe_b64encode/decode and always `.decode('ascii')` when storing. defensive: if you get a `b'='` padding error, try `base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded + '=' * (-len(padded) % 4))`. also add an idempotency key on page fetch so retries don't double-consume a cursor position.

 olivia: agree on idempotency + shape guard. small nit: include explicit model name in telemetry for quicker debugging (we added `model_name` tag on embed calls).

 maria: perfect — pinging @julia for review on the guard + cursor fix. will roll out to staging after merge. thanks y'all :tada:

 julia: on it, will take a look tonight and leave small comments.
